title: Geometric irreducibility of the affine Bertini function field
statement: Let k be a field and A a finite type k-domain, K=Frac A, n>=2 and g_1,...,g_n in A. Suppose V(g_1,g_2) in Spec A has an irreducible component W with dim W+2=dim A. Suppose Spec K is geometrically irreducible over k. Then Omega=Frac(K[x_1,...,x_n]) is geometrically irreducible over F=k(x_1,...,x_n,sum_i g_i x_i). Here finite type, dimensions, components, polynomial rings and field extensions use [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], [def-weil-irreducible-components], [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and [def-pc-field-extension]. F and Omega are the concrete bertiniBaseField and bertiniOmega of [lem-zl-bertini-field-extension]. Conventions: geometric irreducibility [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible].

proof.text: Apply the independent-functions theorem to the component of dimension dim A minus two. Reindex its Fin n plus Fin 2 family by finSumFinEquiv to the Fin (n+2) family used by the field-extension theorem; compare the two final entries by map_sum, map_mul and scalar-tower identities.

The fraction field of A is essentially of finite type over k, hence finitely generated as an intermediate field. Apply the algebraic Bertini theorem with this finite generation, the given geometric irreducibility and the reindexed independent family.

lean.statement:
theorem geometricallyIrreducible_bertiniAffineFunctionField
    (k A : Type u) [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    [Algebra.FiniteType k A] [IsDomain A]
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (g : Fin n → A)
    (hcomp : ∃ W : Set (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus
        ({g ⟨0, Nat.zero_lt_of_lt hn⟩, g ⟨1, hn⟩} : Set A)),
      W ∈ irreducibleComponents (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus
        ({g ⟨0, Nat.zero_lt_of_lt hn⟩, g ⟨1, hn⟩} : Set A)) ∧
      topologicalKrullDim W + 2 = ringKrullDim A)
    (hgeom : GeometricallyIrreducible
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (FractionRing A))))) :
    GeometricallyIrreducible
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
        (algebraMap
          (bertiniBaseField k (FractionRing A) n (fun i ↦ algebraMap A (FractionRing A) (g i)))
          (bertiniOmega (FractionRing A) n))))
